text:
jessica-cs: Heads-up — FortuneLabs escalated. Their streaming job disconnects mid-generation when their auth token refreshes, then reconnects and we see duplicate partial outputs and double billing. Customer sent logs + minimal repro. Can eng help triage?
rahul-eng: looking now. do we have the raw stream events and headers? any 401s?
mila-support: pasted the sanitized log FortuneLabs provided: 
```
[2026-02-12T15:04:10Z] SSE open -> stream_id=stk_abc123 auth=Bearer eyJ... (expires in 300s)
[2026-02-12T15:07:05Z] 401 Unauthorized -> reason: token_expired
[2026-02-12T15:07:05Z] client reconnect attempt using new token
[2026-02-12T15:07:06Z] SSE open -> stream_id=stk_abc123 auth=Bearer eyJ...new
[2026-02-12T15:07:06Z] generation: chunk:start id=gen_789
[2026-02-12T15:07:07Z] generation: chunk:partial id=gen_789 text="The quick brown"
[2026-02-12T15:07:08Z] generation: chunk:partial id=gen_790 text=" jumps over"
[2026-02-12T15:07:09Z] generation: chunk:final id=gen_790 text=" the lazy dog"
```
Note the ID flip from gen_789 -> gen_790 and two partials for overlapping content. Also they report being billed for both sequences.
jessica-cs: They say client SDK v0.9.2 (node) with default reconnect behavior — immediate reconnect on 401.
rahul-eng: hmm. looks like when the same stream_id is reused we should be resuming instead of starting a fresh generation. but gen ids changed after reconnect — server started a new generation in the same session. that can produce duplicate tokens if client double-sends.
sam-qa: quick repro steps they gave: 
1) start SSE stream with token that expires in 5m
2) cause server clock drift / simulate expiry at ~3m
3) client receives 401, refreshes token and reopens SSE using same stream_id header
4) new connection starts a generation before previous generation state cleaned up -> duplicates
I was able to repro locally with a short script.
rahul-eng: thanks. couple hypotheses: 1) if the backend invalidates the session on 401 but doesn't persist the prior generation checkpoint, a reconnect with new auth triggers a fresh generation. 2) client resend of the prompt on reconnect without using an idempotency key can also create a duplicate.
mila-support: customer is anxious about double billing. they want a mitigation asap. any short-term client-side workaround we can recommend?
rahul-eng: short term: set client to backoff on 401 for ~200-500ms before reconnecting, and include an explicit idempotency-key header on the create request (we support `Idempotency-Key`). Also pass `resume_token` if using our resume API so server knows to continue. Code snippet: 
```
// pseudocode
fetch(streamUrl, {headers: {Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'Idempotency-Key': iid}})
.on('error', (e)=>{
  if (e.status === 401) setTimeout(()=>reconnect(), 300)
})
```
sam-qa: we should also tell them to upgrade SDK; v0.9.4 has a resume-token helper and better 401 handling.
infra-bot: deploy 2026-02-14T03:00 -> added resume-window=10s and idempotency checks for reconnect flows to canary.
rahul-eng: long-term server fix: we need to treat a reconnect with the same `stream_id` + valid `resume_token` as a resume, even if auth changed during a short grace window. implementation: persist per-session last-generation-id and accept resume if reconnect within X seconds (configurable). also guard against partial double-append by deduping generation ids server-side.
mila-support: client asked if we can refund the duplicate charge — what's the process?
jessica-cs: I'll open a billing ticket. for immediate relief we can offer a one-time credit while we investigate. please collect the two billing event IDs from the customer's invoice and attach.
rahul-eng: for reproduction artifacts, please ask customer to capture: full SSE headers (stream_id, resume_token if present), the exact Authorization header times (redact token), and the SDK version + minimal script. with that we can correlate server logs and see whether the old generation finished after reconnect or both ran concurrently.
sam-qa: I'll prepare a short KB for CS with recommended client config: upgrade SDK, enable resume_token, add Idempotency-Key, backoff on 401, and avoid immediate re-sending of the same prompt until final event.
mila-support: told FortuneLabs the short-term mitigations and asked for logs. they replied they can repro and will share sanitized headers.
rahul-eng: action items: (1) QA to verify canary resume-window change (sam), (2) eng to add server-side dedupe by generation-id and extend resume grace for token-rotate flows (rahul), (3) CS to collect billing IDs and apply credit if warranted (jessica). I'll also add an internal note to check metrics for recent duplicate-generation errors.
jessica-cs: thanks all. I'll update the customer thread after billing ticket + KB are ready. :thumbsup:
